candidates_considered.name: Solex Energy Ltd
candidates_considered.verdict: RESEARCHED, NOT PUBLISHED - the trigger fails both measured order tests and the press release overstates it. All five of its order filings since its 13-Aug-2026 BSE listing were opened. Today's NEW order is Rs 180.98 cr incl GST, won by subsidiary Solex Green Energy for TOPCon bifacial G2G modules, delivery to January 2027. The press release headline of 'Rs 194.14 Crore Combined Work Orders' adds back the parent's Rs 13.16 cr order that the company had ALREADY filed separately the previous evening (05-Oct-2026 21:01 IST) - so the day's new business is Rs 180.98 cr, not Rs 194.14 cr. Against FY26 net sales of Rs 1,618.06 cr that is 11.2% - the weak bucket (<25% of sales, 21.4% reached 2x in two years vs 35.7% for 25-50%) - and it adds 5.3% to an order book the company already puts at about Rs 3,400 cr. On rarity it is firmly a serial filer: Rs 42.47 cr (13-Aug), Rs 74.77 cr (03-Sep), Rs 75.96 cr (03-Oct), Rs 13.16 cr (05-Oct) and Rs 180.98 cr (06-Oct) = Rs 387.34 cr across five BSE filings in eight weeks, plus a Rs 628.37 cr July order and a Rs 175 cr LOI named in the Q1 presentation. Earnings are going the wrong way: Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 8.26 cr, DOWN 66.6% YoY, EBITDA margin 12.7% from 16.4%, and FY27 utilisation guided DOWN to about 55% from about 70% in FY26 after the late-May ALMM/ALCM timeline clarification put buyers in wait-and-watch. The Rs 1,050 cr 2.2 GW cell line is unfunded: Rs 700 cr of debt 'at an advanced stage of discussion', Rs 350 cr of NCD/CCD equity 'progressing through due diligence', on net debt/equity already 0.57x. See `watch` - the valuation is the reason to come back, not this order.

govt_considered.release: Cabinet approves Commitment of Rs.10,000 Crore towards establishment of the SME Growth Fund for direct equity investments in Small and Medium Enterprises to create future champions
govt_considered.verdict: NOT MAPPED, NOT RESEARCHED, NO NAME ADDED. This is the day's one large-but-unmapped decision and it is above the floor at Rs 10,000 cr, so the gate was right to surface it. But on what the title itself states, the money is a commitment to a FUND making DIRECT EQUITY INVESTMENTS in small and medium enterprises - it is growth capital for (overwhelmingly unlisted) SMEs, not procurement and not an outlay that becomes anybody's order book. That is exactly the distinction this page's own measured history turns on: the programmes that paid were the ones that landed in an order book (defence 17.4x, shipbuilding 16.2x, RDSS smart meters 12.0x), while PM Surya Ghar - a household subsidy, money that did not become an order book - returned 1.8x against the market's 2.0x and produced no 5x at all. An equity fund is further from an order book than a subsidy is. A listed beneficiary class could be argued (SME-focused merchant bankers, NBFCs), but that would be a hunch: no company's own filing was read this run showing this programme is material to it, and the playbook forbids adding a name to theme_map.json on anything less. The release BODY could not be read either - pib.gov.in is blocked from this sandbox and govt.py stores only the title and the matched amount for an unmapped release - so which agency administers the fund, and whether any listed entity is named as a manager or channel, is UNKNOWN. Re-open if a listed company files a disclosure naming this fund.

New business today is Rs 180.98 cr, not the Rs 194.14 cr headline, which adds back the Rs 13.16 cr order already filed the previous evening - 11.2% of FY26 net sales of Rs 1,618.06 cr (the weak band) and 5.3% of an existing ~Rs 3,400 cr order book, from a filer with five BSE order announcements in eight weeks plus a Rs 628.37 cr July order. Q1 FY27 PAT fell 66.6% YoY, FY27 utilisation is guided down to ~55% from ~70%, and the Rs 1,050 cr cell line's Rs 700 cr debt and Rs 350 cr NCD/CCD equity are both unclosed on 0.57x net debt/equity. The valuation is interesting (see watch); this order is not the reason to act on it.

watch: Solex Energy (544862) on valuation rather than on an order. Not published today because the order fails both measured tests, but the numbers read this run are worth returning to: FY26 net sales Rs 1,618.06 cr with PAT Rs 98.25 cr, an order book management puts at about Rs 3,400 cr (2.1x FY26 sales) spread across confirmed POs, signed MSAs and advanced-stage MSAs, 4 GW of module capacity, and a trailing PE of roughly 9x at Rs 690.25 with the stock 22% below its 65-day window high. The business is explicitly H2-weighted and FY28 aspirations are Rs 4,500 cr of revenue at a 5-6% PAT margin. The things that would make it an idea are a Q2 FY27 print showing utilisation moving toward the 55% assumption, and FINANCIAL CLOSE on the cell line (Rs 700 cr debt, Rs 350 cr NCD/CCD). Re-open on either.

note: Three lanes, and this time the filings lane carried the day. GOVERNMENT produced nothing: Actions scanned 41 PIB releases at 18:56 IST and kept zero, with one large-but-unmapped decision - a Rs 10,000 cr Cabinet commitment to an SME Growth Fund for direct equity investments in SMEs. It was surfaced correctly and rejected deliberately: equity capital for mostly unlisted SMEs is not procurement and does not become anybody's order book, which is the exact distinction behind this page's own measured history, where the order-book programmes made 12-17x and PM Surya Ghar's household subsidy returned 1.8x against the market's 2.0x. No name was added to theme_map.json on a hunch. COMMODITY produced no publishable idea either, and two of its findings are worth more than an idea would have been. The sugar group's headline ('spot sugar 1w +23.5%') is a GLOBAL proxy while all eight Indian sugar prints are down 7-16% over a month - so the Dhampur and Avadh Sugar breakouts in the filings lane are NOT the sugar price, and no sugar beneficiary was published. The zinc/lead group mixes a rising metal with a falling one, and its only in-universe name is a lead smelter, so a 4.39 strength resolves to nothing actionable. Of the top three groups by strength, all are driven by WPI at Apr-2026 or the trade panel at 2026-07, and where a fresh Indian print exists it contradicts them. FILINGS produced both ideas, and the run's own re-scan is why there are two: scanning again at 19:59 IST, after the Actions build of 18:58, picked up Om Power's second GETCO LOI (filed 19:41) and Veegaland's investor presentation (19:52, which landed during the scan itself). Om Power Transmission is published on Rs 129.66 cr of GETCO Letters of Intent - 28.9% of a trailing year's sales, the one order ratio the 1,245-filing study found predictive - landing precisely on the metric its own last two disclosures showed falling, at 13.2x trailing and 11.8% below its IPO price, with the eight-filings-in-5.7-months rarity problem published as the main caveat. Veegaland Developers is published on its first reviewed quarter, where revenue, EBITDA, PAT, pre-sales, collections and realisation all moved together, with Rs 431 cr of contracted revenue still to recognise against FY26 sales of Rs 251 cr and the promoter buying in the open market on listing day - capped at medium because thirteen sessions and one quarter cannot meet this page's research standard, and because the company's own first filing contradicts itself twice (note 1 versus note 5 on whether the quarter was reviewed; a realisation slide whose arrows disagree with its own bars). Both contradictions are published rather than smoothed over. Solex Energy was researched and NOT published: its press-release headline of Rs 194.14 cr adds back an order it had already filed the previous evening, the genuinely new Rs 180.98 cr is 11.2% of a trailing year's sales from a filer with five order announcements in eight weeks, and Q1 PAT fell 66.6% - the valuation is interesting enough to carry forward as a watch, but this order was not a reason to publish. Nine further candidates were pure price-and-volume breakouts with no filing, including MobiKwik at +20% on 68x volume and National Fittings at +127% over the window with nothing disclosed at all; all were watch-listed, not researched, exactly as the playbook directs. Two sweeps could not be run: forum.valuepickr.com and cdn.syndication.twimg.com are both refused by this sandbox's egress proxy, so no forum thread was read and no X post body was read by id - what those sources say is unknown, not absent, and every snippet-sourced number that entered a published idea was matched to a primary filing first.
